title: Necessary and sufficient conditions for exact stable inversion of non-minimum phase multivariable systems
author: Burak Kürkçü, Masayoshi Tomizuka
work: Algebraic Control: Complete Stable Inversion with Necessary and Sufficient Conditions
difficulty_reason: The counted theorem is the paper's own necessary and sufficient condition, and the counted proof is not a citation of Exact Model Matching. Supplying the invariant factor theorem, Adapted Forney's theorem, the definition of the RHP zeros and the standing minimality assumption still leaves an argument the author has to build: the rational matrix equation is first cleared of the common denominator, the invariant factor decomposition of the polynomial matrix is used to write down the general solution with its arbitrary RHP-stable vector, and the necessity direction is then split into the full-rank and the rank-deficient case. In the rank-deficient case a minimal polynomial basis has to be produced through a polynomial-unimodular transformation of constant determinant, the pole structure of the control has to be isolated in a scalar denominator, and the vanishing of the output at every RHP zero of the plant has to be extracted by left-multiplying with the left zero direction, which requires knowing that non-singular transformations preserve the invariant zeros. The sufficiency direction runs the same machinery backwards through a factorised control and produces two explicit contradictions at a hypothetical closed right-half-plane pole. Building this equivalence for non-minimum phase, non-square and rank-deficient plants at once is research-level algebraic control theory, well above ordinary PhD qualifying examinations.
